title: AI technology sees through leaves to transform horticulture
excerpt: University of Canterbury (UC) computer science professor Richard Green leads UC Vision, with researcher Dr. Richie Ellingham developing AI and computer vision technology that can identify, measure and track fruit hidden behind dense foliage.
content_html:
University of Canterbury (UC) computer science professor Richard Green leads UC Vision, with researcher Dr. Richie Ellingham developing AI and computer vision technology that can identify, measure and track fruit hidden behind dense foliage.

"You can't automate what you can't see. By creating a complete 3D model of each plant, including what is behind the leaves, we can open the door to automating almost any repetitive manual task associated with that plant," Green says.

He says robots have been used on factory production lines for decades because they work from precise computer-aided design models.

"Agricultural environments are far more complex because every tree, vine, branch and piece of fruit is different."

The UC Vision team's technology addresses that challenge by using cameras, lighting and a complex pipeline of AI systems to digitally remove foliage and reconstruct an accurate 3D model of a plant.

Green says the technology is the first of its kind to create a complete 3D model of individual plants, including fruit and structures hidden behind foliage, to support crop forecasting and future automation.

"The system can identify individual apples, cherries or grapes, show which branch or cane they are attached to, and calculate measurements including their size, volume and surface area. Repeated scans can also track how much an individual piece of fruit has grown."

Green says this information could significantly improve crop forecasting.

"Growers currently rely largely on people to sample, count and measure fruit before harvest, a process that can produce inaccuracies of up to 23%."

The UC technology has achieved fruit counts within about 2% to 3% of the correct figure during testing.

"The result reflects the combined expertise of the research team, including UC researcher Dr. Oliver Batchelor on AI algorithms, Ellingham's mechatronics research and UC research engineer Matt Mattar's development of commercial-quality software alongside specialist research engineers selected for key areas of the project," Green says.

"For large growers, better information could potentially save millions of dollars and reduce waste across their operations.

"Every vineyard and orchard needs to understand how much fruit it will produce and the size distribution of that fruit. Getting that wrong can mean having too many or too few workers, packaging materials or storage resources available at harvest time."

UC Vision has developed mobile camera systems that travel along vineyard and orchard rows. The vineyard system uses two rows of cameras to capture images through dense vine canopies, while a taller camera structure can scan orchard trees reaching approximately 3.5 meters (11.5 feet).

Green says the detailed models could eventually guide autonomous machines to carry out tasks such as pruning, thinning, spraying and harvesting.

"In a cherry orchard, for example, a machine could identify and pick only fruit that had reached the most valuable size, returning later for the remaining crop.

"Cherries that are only a few millimeters larger can be worth twice as much. Selective harvesting could help growers increase the value of their crop while also planning their workforce and packaging requirements more accurately."

The breakthrough builds on about 15 years of UC research projects, supported by more than $32 million in government investment in computer vision, artificial intelligence and agricultural robotics.

The team is now concentrating on making the system highly reliable ahead of potential commercialization through HoloCrop.

Ellingham says the team has collected 3D modeling data across 20 commercial farms to ensure the technology works reliably in real vineyard and orchard conditions.

"Almost every farm we work with is asking when they can start using our sampling tools," Ellingham says.

"HoloCrop is being established to meet demand across the fruit production chain by developing precision horticulture tools that provide more accurate data, reduce food-production waste and support future horticultural robotics."

Green says the technology is the result of years of learning, testing and refinement by an exceptionally talented team.

"We now have technology with the potential to change how food is grown and harvested around the world."

content_html_zh:
坎特伯雷大学 (UC) 计算机科学教授 Richard Green 领导 UC Vision，与研究员 Richie Ellingham 博士一起开发人工智能和计算机视觉技术，可以识别、测量和跟踪隐藏在茂密树叶后面的水果。

“你无法自动化你看不到的东西。 通过创建每株植物的完整 3D 模型，包括叶子后面的内容，我们可以为几乎所有与该植物相关的重复性手动任务实现自动化打开大门，”Green 说。

他说，机器人已经在工厂生产线上使用了几十年，因为它们是根据精确的计算机辅助设计模型工作的。

“农业环境要复杂得多，因为每棵树、藤蔓、树枝和果实都是不同的。”

UC Vision 团队的技术通过使用摄像头、照明和复杂的人工智能系统管道来解决这一挑战，以数字方式去除树叶并重建植物的准确 3D 模型。

Green 表示，该技术是同类技术中第一个创建单个植物的完整 3D 模型的技术，包括果实和隐藏在叶子后面的结构，以支持作物预测和未来的自动化。

“该系统可以识别单个苹果、樱桃或葡萄，显示它们附着在哪个树枝或藤条上，并计算测量值，包括它们的大小、体积和表面积。 重复扫描还可以追踪单个水果的生长情况。”

格林表示，这些信息可以显着改善作物预测。

“目前，种植者主要依靠人工在收获前对水果进行采样、计数和测量，这一过程可能产生高达 23% 的误差。”

在测试过程中，UC 技术的果实计数与正确数字的误差约为 2% 至 3%。

格林说：“结果反映了研究团队的综合专业知识，包括加州大学研究员 Oliver Batchelor 博士在人工智能算法方面的专业知识、Ellingham 的机电一体化研究和加州大学研究工程师马特·马塔 (Matt Mattar) 以及为该项目关键领域挑选的专业研究工程师开发的商业质量软件。”

“对于大型种植者来说，更好的信息可能会节省数百万美元并减少运营过程中的浪费。

“每个葡萄园和果园都需要了解其将生产多少水果以及水果的大小分布。 如果出现错误，可能意味着收获季节可用的工人、包装材料或存储资源过多或过少。”

UC Vision 开发了沿着葡萄园和果园行进的移动摄像系统。 葡萄园系统使用两排摄像机通过茂密的藤蔓树冠捕捉图像，而更高的摄像机结构可以扫描高达约 3.5 米（11.5 英尺）的果园树。

格林表示，详细的模型最终可以指导自动机器执行修剪、间伐、喷洒和收割等任务。

“例如，在樱桃园中，机器可以识别并仅采摘已达到最有价值尺寸的水果，然后返回剩余的作物。

“仅大几毫米的樱桃价值可能是原来的两倍。 选择性收割可以帮助种植者增加作物的价值，同时更准确地规划他们的劳动力和包装要求。”

这一突破建立在加州大学约 15 年的研究项目的基础上，并得到了政府在计算机视觉、人工智能和农业机器人领域超过 3200 万美元的投资的支持。

该团队目前正致力于通过 HoloCrop 实现潜在商业化之前使系统高度可靠。

Ellingham 表示，该团队已经收集了 20 个商业农场的 3D 建模数据，以确保该技术在真实的葡萄园和果园条件下可靠运行。

“几乎每个与我们合作的农场都在询问何时可以开始使用我们的采样工具，”埃林厄姆说。

“HoloCrop 的成立是为了通过开发精密园艺工具来满足整个水果生产链的需求，这些工具可以提供更准确的数据，减少食品生产浪费并支持未来的园艺机器人。”

格林表示，这项技术是一支才华横溢的团队多年学习、测试和完善的结果。

“我们现在拥有的技术有可能改变世界各地粮食的种植和收获方式​​。”
